results.verdict: Yes — an operator can genuinely run VenueOS from an iPhone. This was a real authenticated production run on an isolated SPORTS tenant at an iPhone-class 390x844/touch viewport; all 8 surfaces loaded, were walked, and screenshotted with ZERO console errors and ZERO 5xx/network failures (report.json passed:8 failed:0). Every surface I read has a working bottom tab bar (Home/Assets/Playlists/Screens/More), readable text, thumb-sized tap targets, and no content trapped behind the top header — and notably the two worst historical mobile pains are GONE: the assets media controls are now a compact 'Add URL'/'Upload' button row rather than a floating toolbar over the top nav, and Settings is a clean single-row card stack with no drawer pushing off the left edge. The New Playlist wizard, which used to crash and used to overflow, now opens as a phone-fitted modal with its Cancel/Next buttons visible. The one genuine layout defect I can SEE is on Sports: the 'Game Day' header is a single non-wrapping row, so the '+ New game' button's right edge/rounded corner is clipped at the 390px boundary (verified in a zoomed crop). It is P1 not P0 only because the empty state offers a second fully-visible 'New game' button — but that safety net disappears once any game exists, so the header needs to wrap/stack on narrow widths. The remaining items are P2 polish, dominated by one cross-cutting theme: the global fixed 'Report bug' FAB at bottom-right floats over content on every surface and sits close to right-aligned action buttons (notably Settings' 'Configure' and the AI page's API-key field) — it blocked nothing in the captured frames, but its fixed position means it can occlude controls as pages scroll, and is worth a small inset/auto-hide treatment. Two coverage caveats for honesty: deep multi-step flows (later Playlist wizard steps under the keyboard, and actually opening/editing a template or scoreboard in the builder) were not exercised on the phone in this run, and the builder is historically desktop-heavy, so 'usable on phone' for the core gallery chrome is confirmed but in-builder editing on a phone is unverified here.

results.verdict: Yes — an operator can genuinely run VenueOS from an iPhone (390x844, WebKit/Safari, production venue-os.app). All 8 surfaces loaded with ZERO console errors and ZERO 5xx/network failures, and the historically painful mobile bugs are gone in this capture: on Assets the 'Add URL'/'Upload' buttons sit at the top of the page fully reachable (not a floating toolbar over the top nav), and the main Settings page renders as a tidy single-column card stack with no drawer pushing off the left edge. Dashboard, Screens, Playlists, Templates, Settings and AI are all clean, single-column, no horizontal overflow, with primary actions thumb-reachable and the bottom tab bar usable; the New Playlist wizard opens as a proper full-height modal with its Cancel/Next actions pinned visibly. Two real issues keep it from 'perfect.' (1) The Sports / 'Game Day' header is the one clearly degraded surface — it keeps a desktop side-by-side row instead of stacking on mobile, so the description wraps to ~5 lines in a pinched column and the '+ New game' button is jammed against the right screen edge looking nearly clipped; the task is still doable via the clean empty-state CTA, but the header reads broken (P1, the top fix). (2) The persistent dark bug-reporter FAB at bottom-right overlaps card actions on Templates (it sits over the first template card's 'PREVIEW' pill) and grazes the AI 'Configure' button on Settings — a recurring collision worth giving the FAB more clearance or auto-nudging it off interactive cards (P1/P2). Minor polish: the Assets filter-chip scroller leaves no right-padding so the last 'Documents' chip kisses the edge, and the AI page's Save action sits below the fold. None of these block the core workflows — uploading media, building a playlist, pairing a screen, configuring AI and emergency alerts all complete on the phone — so the verdict is usable-with-two-fixes, with the Sports header being the single most visible thing to repair.

synth.executiveSummary: Yes — an operator can genuinely run the whole product from an iPhone today. Both a Chromium (Android) and a WebKit (iPhone Safari) authenticated production walk loaded all 8 surfaces with zero console errors and zero 5xx/network failures. Dashboard, Screens, Assets, Playlists, Templates, Settings, and AI are all single-column, no horizontal overflow, with thumb-sized targets and a working bottom tab bar; the two worst historical pains are gone (Assets shows a compact Add-URL/Upload row, not a floating toolbar over the nav; Settings is a clean card stack with no left-edge drawer). Core tasks complete: upload media, build a playlist, pair a screen, configure AI and emergency alerts. Two things keep it from perfect: the Sports "Game Day" header doesn't stack on mobile (cramped, "+ New game" jammed/clipped at the right edge), and the global bug-report FAB floats over card actions. Neither blocks the workflows.

p1.issue: The 'Game Day' header is a single non-wrapping desktop flex row (trophy icon + title/description block + 'Sponsors' button + '+ New game' button). On WebKit/iPhone the header does NOT collapse to a stacked layout: the description squeezes into a narrow column and wraps to ~5 lines ('Live / scoreboards, / clocks, and / celebration / cues...'), the buttons vertically center against that tall paragraph, and the '+ New game' primary button's rounded right edge runs hard against the 390px screen boundary with no margin — visibly clipped/nearly clipped and awkward to tap with a right thumb. The task is still completable because the empty state offers a second, fully-visible centered '+ New game' CTA — but that safety net DISAPPEARS once any game exists, at which point the clipped header button becomes the only New-game entry point.
p1.fixHint: Make the Game Day header responsive like Templates/Assets already are: wrap or stack the icon+title block above the action buttons on narrow viewports (flex-col below md), and add right padding/margin so '+ New game' never touches the viewport edge. Confirmed clipped in zoomed crops on both browsers; WebKit shows the worse degraded layout (5-line description wrap).

p1.issue: The persistent dark bug-reporter FAB (bottom-right, position:fixed) overlaps the top-right 'PREVIEW' pill of the first ready-made template card as that card scrolls into the bottom-right corner. At the captured rest position on WebKit the FAB sits directly over that card's Preview control, so tapping Preview on the top card can hit the bug-report FAB instead — a real tap collision at rest, not just a theoretical scroll risk.
p1.fixHint: Give the FAB more clearance (larger bottom inset above the tab bar), auto-hide it on scroll, or nudge it off interactive card regions. Same global-FAB pattern that grazes Settings 'Configure' and the AI key field — fixing the FAB placement once addresses the class.

p2.issue: A persistent dark circular 'Report bug' FAB sits fixed at bottom-right (~90px above the tab bar) on EVERY surface. In the captured frames it blocks nothing on most tabs (floats over whitespace/empty-state cards), but because it is position:fixed it sits close to right-aligned action buttons and can occlude controls as pages scroll — notably Settings' 'Configure' button and the AI page's API-key input/Save area. On WebKit it also overlaps the dashboard 'RIGHT NOW / Screens online' summary card, partially obscuring the right-side count until you scroll.
p2.fixHint: Give the FAB a small inset/auto-hide-on-scroll treatment and keep it clear of right-aligned card actions. One fix covers Dashboard, Settings, AI, Templates collisions.

p2.issue: The filter-chip row (All / Images / Videos / Audio / Urls / Documents) is a single horizontal scroller with no right padding — the last chip 'Documents' ends flush at / kissing the 390px right edge, so it reads as potentially clipped. It IS reachable by swiping the row, but the scroll affordance isn't discoverable at rest.
p2.fixHint: Add right padding / a fade-edge affordance to the scrollable chip row so 'Documents' has breathing room and the horizontal scroll is discoverable.

p2.issue: The API-key input and 'We test the key before saving' helper sit near the bottom of the fold; the primary 'Save key' action is below the fold and requires a scroll — it isn't visible on the first screen.
p2.fixHint: Pin the Save action or pull the key form higher so the primary save button is visible without scrolling on a 390px viewport.

p2.issue: On WebKit the top bar is busy on 390px — hamburger, a truncated tenant pill ('Beta all 178241...'), bell, red emergency shield, and avatar share one row. It fits, but the tenant name is always truncated.
p2.fixHint: Acceptable but tight; consider a slightly more generous tenant-name truncation or moving a secondary icon into the More menu on narrow widths.

Later steps (Step-2/3 media selection with reorder/duration, Step-4 schedule/screen-group picker) were not exercised, so it is unconfirmed whether every step keeps its Cancel/Next actions above the keyboard/fold. Minor WebKit nit: 'Next' is correctly disabled until a name is entered but there's no inline hint that it's gated.
p2.fixHint: Run a dedicated multi-step phone pass through the full wizard with the keyboard open to confirm action buttons stay visible; add an inline hint that Next is gated on a name.

The builder is historically a desktop-heavy surface, so in-builder editing on a phone is unverified.

iphoneSpecific.issue: On WebKit/iPhone the Game Day header is the clearest degraded surface: it keeps a desktop side-by-side row instead of stacking, so the description pinches into a narrow column wrapping to ~5 lines and the buttons vertically center against that tall paragraph — it reads visibly 'broken/cramped'. The Chromium run flagged the same non-wrapping header but emphasized the clipped '+ New game' corner; WebKit additionally exposed the full degraded multi-line layout, which is why WebKit marked the surface usableOnPhone:false while Chromium kept it true.

The bug-report FAB collision is worse on WebKit: at the captured rest position the FAB sits directly over the first template card's 'PREVIEW' pill, so the Preview tap can be intercepted by the FAB. Chromium rated the FAB as P2 (floated over whitespace), but WebKit caught it at rest over an interactive control, elevating it to P1 on iPhone.

WebKit specifically showed the FAB overlapping the 'RIGHT NOW / Screens online' summary card and partially obscuring the right-side count, plus a tight, always-truncated tenant pill in the busy top bar at 390px — observations not called out in the Chromium run.

The 'Save key' action being below the fold (requires scroll) was specifically surfaced in the WebKit walk; the Chromium walk noted the AI page was clean and did not flag the Save position. Same FAB-near-key-field occlusion risk on both.

topThemes: Non-responsive desktop headers on narrow viewports: the Sports 'Game Day' header is a single non-wrapping flex row that doesn't stack, so its '+ New game' button is clipped at the 390px edge — the exact pattern that Templates and Assets headers already solve by wrapping. Several pages already wrap correctly; Sports is the outlier that regressed.

Global fixed 'Report bug' FAB occlusion: a position:fixed FAB at bottom-right recurs on every surface and floats over content, sitting close to (and on WebKit, directly over) right-aligned card actions — Templates' PREVIEW pill, Settings' Configure, the AI key field, the dashboard status card. One placement/auto-hide fix addresses the whole class.

Horizontal chip scrollers with no edge affordance: the Assets filter-chip row runs flush to the right edge ('Documents' kisses 390px) with no right padding or fade, making the horizontal scroll undiscoverable at rest — a discoverability anti-pattern.

Primary actions / content sitting just below or at the fold: AI page 'Save key' below the fold, Screens 'No Screen Groups Yet' header half-cut, first template/sports preview cards only just appearing — vertical budgeting could lift key elements into the first viewport.

Historical mobile pains are confirmed FIXED across both browsers — Assets media controls are now a compact top button row (not a floating toolbar over the nav), Settings is a single-column card stack (no left-edge drawer), and the New Playlist wizard opens as a phone-fitted modal with Cancel/Next pinned — showing the mobile-hardening effort is landing.

Coverage gaps in deep/multi-step flows: later New Playlist wizard steps under the keyboard and actual in-builder template/scoreboard editing on a phone were not exercised in either run, so 'usable on phone' is confirmed for chrome/gallery but unverified for deep editing.
